items.title: CISA confirms attacks on VMware vCenter and Cisco Expressway flaws; patch by Nov. 23
items.why: CISA added four exploited flaws to its KEV list on Friday: VMware vCenter, Cisco Expressway, Apache Roller and SAP NetWeaver. China-linked hackers paired the vCenter bug with a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw.
items.action: Install the November vCenter and Apache Roller fixes and the October Expressway update now, and confirm BeyondTrust Remote Support is fully patched.

items.title: FBI investigates a breach of NCIC, the national crime database police use daily
items.why: The FBI is probing an apparent intrusion into the National Crime Information Center, which agencies use for warrants and background checks. It is the second FBI system breach in recent months; no details on the data taken yet.
items.action: Treat any call or email citing a warrant, background check or police record as suspect, and verify it by calling the agency's published number before acting.

items.title: Fake 'verify you are human' prompts push remote-control malware via ads and hacked sites
items.why: Several ClickFix campaigns trick people into pasting a command that installs remote-access tools, using 70,000 hacked sites, WordPress admin logins and a Google ad for Amazon Business that leads to a fake login page.
items.action: Tell staff that no real website asks them to paste a command into Windows Run or PowerShell, and block or alert on unapproved remote tools like NetSupport.

items.title: Unpatched Windows 11 trick uses Narrator to get past the lock screen
items.why: A researcher released a working exploit, FastUnlock, that abuses the Narrator screen reader to run code from the Windows 11 lock screen. It needs physical access and a Microsoft-linked account. No patch yet.
items.action: Keep laptops physically secured, turn on BitLocker, and watch for Microsoft's fix in the next Windows update; install it as soon as it ships.

items.title: Ruby patches seven flaws, including 'Ruby2Shell' that can reach Rails and Sinatra apps
items.why: Ruby fixed seven bugs in its regex and string code; proof-of-concept code exists for five. Default Rails and Sinatra apps may be reachable without login. GitLab, Mastodon, Discourse and others have patched.
items.action: Update Ruby to 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14, and ask vendors of any Ruby-based web app or GitHub Enterprise Server you run when their patched build ships.

items.title: European Commission confirms an AI-assisted attack took services offline for over 10 days
items.why: The Commission said attackers used an AI tool; its HR, medical claims and translation systems were pulled offline. The Artex AI framework has also been tied to attacks on Barracuda, Railway and ConnectWise customers.
items.action: Patch internet-facing systems within days, not weeks, and remove old vendor and integration keys you no longer use; AI tools are speeding up how fast attackers find gaps.
